title: Babies learn to calm themselves from calm caregivers
summary: CDC says babies learn to calm themselves from caregivers who are calm and who make them feel safe.
body: The CDC 1-year page says babies learn to calm themselves from caregivers who are calm and make them feel safe. The help it names on that line is talking softly, holding, rocking, or singing, and letting the baby suck on fingers or a pacifier. The claim on this card is the learning sentence: settling is picked up from a calm person, not only done to the baby. The page is a US tip sheet. It does not say a baby who is still crying has failed to learn.

sources.title: Milestones by 1 Year

sources.note: US government public domain. Supports the sentence that babies learn to calm themselves from caregivers who are calm and make them feel safe.
